# form of

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:formOf`](gmeow-formOf.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/formOf>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/lexicon`](../../slices/lexicon.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The lexical item that a form is a form of — the inverse of [`gmeow:hasLexicalForm`](gmeow-hasLexicalForm.md).

## Structure

**Property shape:** object property; [`gmeow:LexicalForm`](../classes/gmeow-LexicalForm.md) -> [`gmeow:LexicalItem`](../classes/gmeow-LexicalItem.md)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:formOf`](gmeow-formOf.md) from [`gmeow:LexicalForm`](../classes/gmeow-LexicalForm.md) to [`gmeow:LexicalItem`](../classes/gmeow-LexicalItem.md) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

## Common Companion Terms

[`gmeow:LexicalForm`](../classes/gmeow-LexicalForm.md), [`gmeow:LexicalItem`](../classes/gmeow-LexicalItem.md)

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use from a form's side to name the lexical item it realizes — the natural direction in form-rooted data or projections.

### Avoid when

- Avoid asserting both directions redundantly; prefer [`gmeow:hasLexicalForm`](gmeow-hasLexicalForm.md) from the item and read [`gmeow:formOf`](gmeow-formOf.md) as its inverse.

### How to use

- Assert [`gmeow:formOf`](gmeow-formOf.md) from the [`gmeow:LexicalForm`](../classes/gmeow-LexicalForm.md) to its [`gmeow:LexicalItem`](../classes/gmeow-LexicalItem.md) when the form is the natural subject; tooling reads it as the inverse of [`gmeow:hasLexicalForm`](gmeow-hasLexicalForm.md).

### Examples

- ex:waterWritten [`gmeow:formOf`](gmeow-formOf.md) ex:wordWater.
